questions.stem: Argon is used to fill the space inside incandescent light bulbs rather than using air. Why is argon chosen for this purpose?

options.text: Argon glows brightly when heated, adding to the light output
Argon is unreactive and will not react with the hot tungsten filament, preventing it from burning away
Argon is the lightest noble gas, making the bulb lighter
Argon is a good conductor of electricity, helping the filament heat up

questions.explanation: The tungsten filament in a light bulb reaches temperatures over 2500°C. If oxygen were present, the tungsten would quickly oxidise and burn out. Argon provides an inert atmosphere because it has a full outer electron shell and does not react with the hot filament, extending the bulb's lifespan.

questions.stem: Helium is used in airships and weather balloons instead of hydrogen. What is the main advantage of helium over hydrogen for this use?

options.text: Helium is lighter than hydrogen
Helium provides more lift than hydrogen
Helium is non-flammable and much safer, while hydrogen is highly flammable
Helium is cheaper than hydrogen

questions.explanation: Although hydrogen is slightly lighter and provides marginally more lift, helium is much safer because it is completely unreactive (full outer shell). The Hindenburg disaster in 1937 demonstrated the danger of using flammable hydrogen in airships. Helium, as a noble gas, cannot burn or explode.

questions.stem: The boiling points of the noble gases increase from helium (-269°C) to radon (-62°C). What causes this trend?

options.text: Larger atoms have stronger covalent bonds between them
Larger atoms have more electrons, creating stronger London dispersion forces between atoms
Heavier atoms have stronger ionic bonds
Larger atoms have more protons attracting neighbouring atoms

questions.explanation: Noble gases exist as individual atoms with no chemical bonds between them. The only forces between noble gas atoms are weak London dispersion forces. Larger atoms (going down the group) have more electrons, creating stronger temporary dipoles and therefore stronger London dispersion forces. More energy is needed to overcome these forces, raising the boiling point.

questions.stem: Early versions of the periodic table did not include noble gases. Why were they not discovered until the 1890s?

options.text: They did not exist until the 1890s
They are extremely rare in the Earth's atmosphere
Their extreme unreactivity meant they did not form compounds that could be easily detected by chemical methods
They are invisible to all scientific instruments

questions.explanation: Noble gases are unreactive because they have full outer electron shells. Early chemists identified elements through their chemical reactions and compounds. Since noble gases do not readily form compounds, they were essentially invisible to chemical analysis. It was not until scientists like Rayleigh and Ramsay used physical methods (examining gas densities and spectra) that they were identified.

questions.stem: Neon is used in advertising signs and produces a distinctive red-orange glow. This occurs when electricity passes through neon gas. Which property of noble gases makes them suitable for this application?

options.text: Noble gases are good conductors of electricity
Noble gases emit coloured light when their electrons are excited by electrical energy, and they do not react with the electrodes
Noble gases are the only elements that can produce light
Noble gases are cheap and available in large quantities

questions.explanation: When electricity passes through noble gases at low pressure, electrons absorb energy and move to higher energy levels. When they drop back down, they emit light of characteristic colours. Neon gives red-orange, while other noble gases give different colours. Their unreactivity is also important — they will not corrode the electrodes inside the tube.
